# Model fixtures

`c-mixture-occupancy.txt` was generated by `tests/reference/mixture_occupancy_oracle.c` against the pinned unmodified Debug C build. Its 96 records cover HSMM/HMM calculation modes, temperatures 0.5 and 1, one/two/three components with nonuniform weights, permuted emission-state mappings, zero state occupancies, and absent pruned slices. Every component value must match binary32 exactly.

`corrected-c-duration-occupancy.txt` has 192 records covering all four HSMM scenarios used by `c-hsmm.txt`. It is generated by compiling `tests/reference/hsmm_oracle.c` with `-DDURATION_ORACLE`, a copy of the pinned `inference.c` with only `tests/reference/duration-initialization.patch` applied, and the existing upstream archive. The copied inference source supplies all inference symbols, so the archive's unmodified inference object is not linked. It covers trimmed duration slices and normalized state occupancies with exact binary32 comparisons. The initialization correction is intentional and disclosed; this fixture is not described as unmodified C output.

`c-transitions.txt` covers incoming jump order, nonunit transition weights, self/skip/backward jumps, ignored out-of-range destinations, and two successive calls to the original jump builder. Rust compares all 16 records against `tests/reference/transition_oracle.c`.

`c-hsmm.txt` comes from `tests/reference/hsmm_oracle.c` against the pinned Debug C library. Four scenarios provide 192 records containing forward and backward begin/end scores and their Viterbi paths. They vary annealing and pruning, use duration floors and ceilings, and include a forced best path `0, 2, 1, 1, 2, 3` covering skips, backward jumps, and repeated states. All listed forward scores and path boundaries must match exactly. The original Viterbi optional score-output branch is not invoked because it contains an invalid pointer write; Rust's Viterbi score tables still need an independent reference check beyond the verified path. HSMM duration and state occupancy are not covered yet.

`c-geometric.txt` was generated by `tests/reference/geometric_oracle.c` against the pinned Debug C build. The 384 records cover one-frame/one-state and twelve-frame/three-state HMMs, temperature multipliers 0.5 and 1, two pruning slopes, duration means below the original 1.01 clamp, forward/backward scores, Viterbi scores and boundaries, all three total helpers, 64 quantized numerical-helper cases, and 146 state/transition occupancy records. The occupancy checks include excluded endpoint frames and absent transition slices. Exact binary32 equality is required for these fixtures.

`src/lse-table.bin` and `src/exp-table.bin` preserve the 7,000 published values of each upstream `math-funcs.c` table as little-endian binary32. Reproduce them with `tools/extract-probability-tables.ps1 -SourcePath <upstream>/math-funcs.c -OutputDirectory <crate>/src`. The source tables are covered by liblrhsmm's GPL-3.0-or-later notice; they are algorithm coefficients rather than trained model data.

`c-emission-tables.txt` comes from `tests/reference/emission_table_oracle.c` with the same pinned Debug C build. Its 72 records cover 12 frames, three states, two streams with different dimensions and mixture counts, nonunit stream weights, and both original pruning methods. Tests check every value, including excluded-state sentinels and inclusive segment boundaries. Release `-Ofast` inference comparisons remain pending.

`c-emissions.txt` was generated by `tests/reference/emission_oracle.c` using the pinned current C library with `FP_TYPE=float` and the Debug configuration. The 24 cases cover one, two, and three Gaussian components, two DAEM temperature multipliers, and near/far observations including approximate exponential underflow. The tests require exact binary32 agreement for component and mixture log densities and approximate densities. This evidence covers the listed cases, not the complete inference algorithms.

`c-parameters.txt` was generated by `tests/reference/parameter_oracle.c` against the same pinned current C library, with `FP_TYPE=float` and the default Debug build. It covers minimum-duration rejection, weighted normal log density above and below the search maximum, and repeated mixture splitting with nonzero variance floors. Rust tests require exact binary32 equality after parsing the nine-significant-digit output. This criterion applies to these cases, not to all future inference or training calculations.

`cmu-arctic-all-speakers.hsmm` is copied unchanged from SHIRO commit `203ef7b71bf382c8b5ce3f86b8116f63265e2711`. SHA-256: `5e5b56996817c058296a50e13b9719a928fd197ecdfb6341b139eeab604520f1`.

This fixture predates liblrhsmm's GMM variance-floor addition. The original C serializer from `55139ce1fa14381bbb53c21fd6195d36b8f18619`, compiled against the current headers and model implementation, reads and rewrites it with identical bytes. This is a historical serialization oracle, not a complete historical inference build.

`current-c-model.hsmm` was produced by reading the Rust-generated current-format version with the unmodified current C `lrh_read_model` and rewriting it with `lrh_write_model` at commit `1df92da4b77377f4725509e7240a9107ed4c063b`. SHA-256: `2467701cd9732eb702819d7418100d499966ea5f02fdc57977ea63a31cc00743`.

Both models contain three streams and 215 duration distributions. The Rust tests compare every decoded field and both output byte sequences. The test also bounds hostile array sizes and rejects truncated input and trailing objects.

The current C reader rejects the historical fixture at byte offset 23 because it expects three values per GMM dimension rather than two. This is evidence for supporting both layouts in Rust, not a reason to replace the pretrained model.

The four `c-observation*.bin` and `c-segmentation*.bin` files were generated by the current C serializers using `tests/reference/data_oracle.c`. They cover time-major multistream observations, state boundaries, skip/self/backward transitions, and nested datasets. The C reader also verified the generated nested segmentation set. Rust tests compare decoded fields and reproduce each fixture byte for byte, including the legacy segmentation array-header mismatches.

`tests/reference/model_oracle.c` is the reference driver. Build the upstream C library with `make`, then compile the driver with `-DFP_TYPE=float -std=c99 -I<upstream> <driver> <upstream>/build/liblrhsmm.a -lm`. To run the historical serializer, obtain `serial.c` from the historical commit and compile it before the static archive using the current upstream include directory.

The c-updates.txt fixture contains 12 records from tests/reference/update_oracle.c against the pinned unmodified Debug C library. It covers normal and geometric duration updates, duration and emission floors, and low state/component occupancy. The c-initialization.txt fixture contains six records from tests/reference/initialization_oracle.c, covering two streams, shared states, a zero-length segment, and repeated accumulation. Both require exact binary32 equality. Fixed-mean variance, long-duration integer overflow, and atomic failure regressions are independent Rust tests because those behaviors intentionally correct upstream defects.

corrected-c-estimation.txt contains 40 records from tests/reference/estimation_oracle.c. It uses the pinned Debug C library with the disclosed one-line duration initialization correction in tests/reference/duration-initialization.patch; geometric estimation does not call that corrected operation. Cases cover HSMM and geometric HMM expectation collection with two streams, single/multi-component emissions, permuted emission states, two temperatures, and both pruning conventions. Every likelihood and sufficient-statistic value must match exactly. The driver resets the duration normalizer sentinel before each independent case to rebuild the upstream temperature-dependent duration cache.

The six corrected-c-regroup-*-*.bin files come from tests/reference/regroup_oracle.c linked with the pinned Debug C library and the data.c correction recorded in tests/reference/data-regroup.patch. They cover two feature streams, five states grouped by two, a zero-length state, and a final short group. c-resegmentation.bin uses the unmodified lrh_seg_shuffle function and covers skips, repeated states, and backward selection. Tests compare decoded fields and serialized bytes, then independently reconstruct every source frame for unit sizes 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, and usize::MAX.

The c-standalone-duration.bin, c-standalone-gmm.bin, and c-standalone-stream.bin fixtures are produced and reread by the pinned unmodified Debug C serializers using tests/reference/standalone_oracle.c. They cover duration constraints and floors, one/two-component mixtures, mixture-major parameters, and a nonunit stream weight. Standalone Rust serialization must reproduce each fixture byte for byte. Historical standalone layouts are also checked for Rust round trips and rejection of unrepresentable nonzero floors; the historical C reader is not invoked by this driver.

c-generation.txt comes from tests/reference/generation_oracle.c, the pinned unmodified generate.c, and the pinned Debug C archive. The driver replaces rand() with a controlled six-value cycle; all model, selection, and sampling algorithms remain unchanged. The driver and generate.c are compiled with -O2 to inline the upstream fasttrig C functions, whose unoptimized external-inline symbols do not link from the Debug archive. No -Ofast or -ffast-math is used. Twenty-two records cover Gaussian draws, strict cumulative mixture selection and last-index fallback, two-stream variable-mixture generation, zero variances, duration clamping, ignored generation duration constraints, sampled boundaries, feature values, and total draw counts. Every compared binary32 value is exact. Seeded SmallRng tests verify repeatability within a target; they do not assert cross-platform seed equivalence.

c-probability-forms.txt contains 54 records from tests/reference/probability_forms_oracle.c against the pinned unmodified Debug C archive. Eighteen records compare annealed duration log densities and densities at two temperatures, including minimum rejection and values above the search maximum. Thirty-six records compare non-log multistream emission values with inclusive boundary pruning. Each value must match binary32 exactly; C duration densities are returned as double but contain a promoted binary32 approximate-exponential result. The reference resets duration cache preparation between temperatures.

c-construction-model.hsmm and c-copy-*.bin are produced by tests/reference/construction_oracle.c against the pinned unmodified Debug C library. The initial model covers two streams, mixed component/dimension counts, zero moments/floors, uniform weights, and unset duration constraints. The GMM and segmentation fixtures are copied by the original C copy functions before the source is modified; variance floors and skip/self transition weights are preserved. The dataset fixture copies two references to the same source into two independent owned segmentations. Rust tests reproduce every fixture byte for byte and verify independent cloned storage.
